name: Mysuru Heritage Core
short_description: The royal seat of the Wadiyar dynasty featuring the Indo-Saracenic Mysore Palace, Chamundi Hill, and Devaraja Market.
how_to_reach: Major railhead and highway junction; well connected to Bengaluru via the Expressway and Shatabdi trains.
heritage_era: Wadiyar Dynasty (14th–20th century CE)
local_craft: Rosewood inlay woodwork, Mysore silk saris, and sandalwood carving
cultural_note: The city's cultural rhythm is anchored by the centuries-old Dasara tradition initiated by Raja Wadiyar in 1610.

festivals.name: Mysuru Dasara
festivals.note: Ten-day state festival (Nada Habba) culminating in the Jamboo Savari elephant procession from the Palace.

phrases.english: Can we take photos inside the palace?
phrases.when_to_use: At ticket counters and entry checkpoints.

name: Somanathapura
short_description: A pristine trikuta (triple-shrined) Hoysala temple dedicated to Prasanna Chennakeshava, built by Dandanayaka Somanatha.
how_to_reach: Located ~38 km east of Mysuru city along the Kaveri river plains; best reached by taxi or bus via Bannur.
heritage_era: Hoysala Empire (1268 CE, King Narasimha III)
local_craft: Miniature soapstone carving replicas sold near temple gates
cultural_note: UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2023 as part of the Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas.

phrases.kannada: ದೇವಾಲಯದ ಕೆತ್ತನೆಗಳನ್ನು ನೋಡಲು ಎಷ್ಟು ಸಮಯ ಬೇಕು?
phrases.transliteration: Devaalayada kettanegalannu noodalu eshtu samaya beku?
phrases.english: How much time is needed to see temple carvings?
phrases.when_to_use: Planning your visit at the entrance.

name: Melkote
short_description: Sacred hill town and centre of Srivaishnavism, home to Cheluvanarayana Swamy Temple, hilltop Yoga Narasimha shrine, and Akka-Thangi Kalyani.
how_to_reach: Approximately 50 km from Mysuru and 130 km from Bengaluru via the Mandya/Pandavapura turnoff.
heritage_era: Hoysala, Vijayanagara & Wadiyar (12th–18th century CE)
local_craft: Traditional handloom weaving and brass lamp casting
cultural_note: Philosopher Sri Ramanujacharya resided here for twelve years in the early 12th century.

festivals.name: Vairamudi Brahmotsava
festivals.note: Famous annual night procession where the deity is adorned with the historic diamond crown.

phrases.english: Where can we get Puliyogare prasaada?

name: Channapatna
short_description: The Gombegala Ooru (City of Toys), famous for GI-tagged lacquerware turned from Wrightia tinctoria (Aale Mara) softwood using vegetable dyes.
how_to_reach: Located on the Bengaluru–Mysuru highway corridor; easily reached by KSRTC buses or local train.
heritage_era: Late 18th century CE craft guilds onwards
local_craft: GI-tagged lacquerware wooden toys, rocking horses, and educational beads
cultural_note: Tipu Sultan invited Persian master craftsmen to train local artisans in lacquerware woodturning.

phrases.english: How are wooden toys made?

name: Basaralu
short_description: An offbeat rural village housing the 13th-century Mallikarjuna Temple with intricate exterior friezes depicting Ramayana panels.
how_to_reach: ~25 km north of Mandya town; accessible via local country roads by private vehicle or rural bus.
heritage_era: Hoysala Empire (1234 CE, King Vira Narasimha II)
local_craft: Rural pottery and coconut palm leaf weaving
cultural_note: Commissioned by Harihara Dandanayaka, the temple showcases exquisite multi-layered base friezes with war elephants and makaras.

phrases.english: Who has the temple keys?
phrases.when_to_use: When visiting off-peak hours in rural villages.

name: Govindanahalli
short_description: A rare and remarkable panchalingeshwara (five-shrined) Hoysala stone temple aligned along a single grand porch, set amid quiet green fields.
how_to_reach: Near Kikkeri and K.R. Pet in Mandya district, ~65 km from Mysuru.
heritage_era: Hoysala Empire (1237 CE, King Vira Someshwara)
local_craft: Sericulture and silk cocoon rearing in nearby villages
cultural_note: Attributed to master sculptor Ruvari Mallitamma, this is the only surviving intact quintuple-temple plan in Hoysala architecture.

phrases.english: Is this the temple with five sanctums?

name: Aralaguppe
short_description: Ancient village home to the 9th-century Nolamba Kallesvara Temple with remarkable ceiling sculptures of dancing Nataraja.
how_to_reach: Located ~60 km from Tumakuru and ~18 km from Tiptur; accessible by rural train or local roads.
heritage_era: Nolamba Dynasty & Hoysala Empire (9th–13th century CE)
local_craft: Coir processing and coconut fibre handicrafts around Tiptur
cultural_note: The central ceiling bhuvaneshwari slab features Ashta-Dikpalas and dancing Shiva, considered a pinnacle of Nolamba stone sculpting.

phrases.english: Please show us the ceiling sculptures

name: Kaidala
short_description: Historical village historically known as Kridapura, featuring a towering 6-foot monolithic idol of Chennakeshava attributed to master sculptor Jakanachari.
how_to_reach: Situated ~9 km south of Tumakuru city; easily reached by auto-rickshaw or taxi.
heritage_era: Hoysala & Vijayanagara (12th–14th century CE)
local_craft: Black stone idol carving tradition
cultural_note: Folklore tells that legendary sculptor Jakanachari regained his severed right hand here after completing the Chennakeshava idol.

phrases.english: What is the story of Jakanachari?

name: Talakadu
short_description: Mysterious riverside settlement on the Kaveri bends where historic temples like Vaidyanatheshwara and Keerthinarayana are excavated from creeping sand dunes.
how_to_reach: ~45 km from Mysuru via T. Narasipura; connected by state buses and cabs.
heritage_era: Western Ganga, Chola & Hoysala (10th–14th century CE)
local_craft: Coracle boat building and bamboo fishing traps
cultural_note: Known for the famous historical curse of Alamelamma associated with the fall of the Vijayanagara viceroys.

festivals.name: Panchalinga Darshana
festivals.note: Occasional sacred pilgrimage cycle calculated on rare astrological alignments.

phrases.english: Where are the temples buried in the sand?

name: Shravanabelagola
short_description: World-renowned Jain pilgrimage centre featuring the 57-foot monolithic statue of Lord Bahubali atop Vindhyagiri hill.
how_to_reach: Located ~80 km from Mysuru and 140 km from Bengaluru; connected by Shravanabelagola railway station.
heritage_era: Western Ganga Dynasty (981 CE, Chavundaraya)
local_craft: Brass and copper pooja vessels craft in the town bazaar
cultural_note: The Vindhyagiri and Chandragiri hills hold over 800 rock inscriptions detailing the history of Kannada literature.

festivals.name: Mahamastakabhisheka
festivals.note: Grand head-anointing ceremony performed once every 12 years.

phrases.english: How many steps are there to climb the hill?
phrases.when_to_use: At the foot of Vindhyagiri (approx. 650 steps).

name: Ranganathittu
short_description: Six islets on the Kaveri River that form Karnataka's largest bird sanctuary, famous for nesting painted storks and marsh crocodiles.
how_to_reach: ~16 km north of Mysuru near Srirangapatna; easily accessed via highway cabs or local buses.
heritage_era: Protected Wildlife Wetland (1940 onwards)
local_craft: Local river reed baskets
cultural_note: Dr. Salim Ali surveyed the islets in 1940 and persuaded the Maharaja of Mysore to declare the area a sanctuary.

phrases.english: Where can we get tickets for the boat ride?

name: Shivanasamudra
short_description: The twin roaring waterfalls of Gaganachukki and Bharachukki where the Kaveri river plunges over rocky crags, site of India's earliest hydroelectric plant.
how_to_reach: ~75 km east of Mysuru and 130 km from Bengaluru via Malavalli.
heritage_era: Early 20th century hydroelectric heritage (1902 CE) & Ancient shrines
local_craft: Coracle boating tradition along the rocky pools
cultural_note: The Shivanasamudra hydro station, commissioned by Diwan K. Seshadri Iyer in 1902, supplied electricity to Kolar Gold Fields.

phrases.english: How far is it between Bharachukki and Gaganachukki?

name: Biligirirangana Hills
short_description: Biogeographical bridge linking the Western and Eastern Ghats, revered for the clifftop Biligiriranganatha Swamy Temple and Soliga tribal heritage.
how_to_reach: ~85 km south-east of Mysuru and 40 km from Chamarajanagar railhead.
heritage_era: Ganga & Hoysala sacred tradition; Soliga indigenous territory
local_craft: Soliga tribal non-timber forest produce and medicinal root mixtures
cultural_note: The Soliga tribe regards the champaka tree (Dodda Sampige) as sacred and has co-existed with tigers for centuries.

phrases.kannada: ದೊಡ್ಡ ಸಂಪಿಗೆ ಮರ ಎಷ್ಟು ದೂರ ಇದೆ?
phrases.transliteration: Dodda sampige mara eshtu doora ide?
phrases.english: How far is the ancient Champaka tree?

name: Gundlupet Flower Fields
short_description: The gateway to the Nilgiri slopes, known for vast golden sunflower and marigold flower valleys and rural farm trails.
how_to_reach: ~60 km south of Mysuru along NH 766 towards Wayanad and Ooty.
heritage_era: Wadiyar border trade town and ancient Hoysala outpost
local_craft: Terracotta rustic cookware
cultural_note: Gundlupet flower fields bloom between July and September, forming a yellow carpet against the blue mountains.

phrases.english: Which is the road to the sunflower farms?

name: Maravanthe
short_description: Scenic stretch where NH 66 runs between the Arabian Sea on one side and the Souparnika River on the other.
how_to_reach: Located along NH 66, ~12 km north of Kundapura and ~50 km from Udupi.
local_craft: Coastal coir matting and traditional fishing net knotting
cultural_note: Local fishing families venerate the sea through annual Ganga Pooja rituals before the monsoon fishing resumption.

phrases.kannada: ಇಲ್ಲಿ ಸೂರ್ಯಾಸ್ತ ನೋಡಲು ಉತ್ತಮ ಜಾಗ ಯಾವುದು?
phrases.transliteration: Illi sooryaasta noodalu uttama jaaga yaavudu?
phrases.english: Where is the best spot to watch the sunset here?

name: Barkur
short_description: Ancient royal capital of the Alupa dynasty, boasting stone-roofed Panchalingeshwara and Batta Vinayaka temples, Jain basadis, and coastal ruins.
how_to_reach: ~16 km north of Udupi and ~4 km from Brahmavara off NH 66.
heritage_era: Alupa Dynasty & Vijayanagara (7th–14th century CE)
local_craft: Granite stone idol masonry and wood carvings for coastal Daivastana shrines
cultural_note: Barkur was known in antiquity as Barakanur and was celebrated for having 365 temples, allowing the king to visit one every day of the year.

phrases.english: Where is the old Alupa fort?

name: Moodabidri
short_description: The Jain Kashi of the South, renowned for the 15th-century Saavira Kambada Basadi (Thousand Pillar Temple) and palm-leaf manuscripts.
how_to_reach: ~35 km northeast of Mangaluru city; easily accessed by frequent KSRTC and private buses.
heritage_era: Vijayanagara & Chowta Dynasty (15th century CE)
local_food: Shevai (rice noodles) with sweetened coconut milk
local_craft: Palm-leaf manuscript preservation and stone carving
cultural_note: The Thousand Pillar Temple is noted for never having two identical pillars across its expansive stepped hall.

phrases.english: How do we get to the Thousand Pillar Basadi?

name: Gokarna
short_description: Pilgrimage town set along cliff-backed beaches, famous for the revered Mahabaleshwar Atmalinga temple, Om Beach, and Kudle Beach.
how_to_reach: Located along the coast with Gokarna Road railway station on the Konkan Railway; buses connect from Karwar and Kumta.
heritage_era: Kadamba & Vijayanagara sacred coastal history (4th–16th century CE)
local_craft: Sea-shell jewellery and brass pooja bells
cultural_note: Associated with the legend of Ravana carrying the Atmalinga given by Lord Shiva; the linga was set down here by Ganesha disguised as a cowherd.

festivals.name: Maha Shivaratri
festivals.note: Major annual temple car festival when thousands of pilgrims pull two large temple chariots down Car Street.

phrases.english: Can we walk to Om Beach from here?
phrases.when_to_use: Asking about the cliff-side trekking path.

name: Mirjan Fort
short_description: Atmospheric 16th-century laterite fort with high crenellated bastions, secret wells, and moats on the banks of the Aghanashini River.
how_to_reach: ~11 km from Kumta and ~22 km from Gokarna just off NH 66.
heritage_era: Gersoppa Nayaka Dynasty (Queen Chennabhairadevi, 16th century CE)
local_craft: Laterite stone block dressing
cultural_note: Built by Queen Chennabhairadevi, known to Portuguese traders as the 'Pepper Queen' for her control of spice trade through Gersoppa.

phrases.english: Who built the walls of this fort?

name: Yana Rocks
short_description: Towering monolithic karst black limestone rock formations (Bhairaveshwara Shikhara and Mohini Shikhara) hidden inside dense evergreen forests.
how_to_reach: ~28 km from Kumta and ~40 km from Sirsi; requires a 1.5 km forest trail walk from the parking area.
heritage_era: Geological Karst Formation & Ancient cave shrine
local_craft: Bamboo walking sticks crafted by forest dwellers
cultural_note: Mythology links the black soot-colored rocks to the ashes of demon Bhasmasura, burnt by Mohini's cosmic dance.

festivals.name: Yana Shivaratri Jathre
festivals.note: Annual gathering when pilgrims visit the cave shrine dripping with natural cave water.

phrases.english: Is there a path to enter the cave?
phrases.when_to_use: Before entering the limestone fissure trail.

name: Karkala
short_description: Historic town home to the 42-foot monolithic Gommateshwara statue on Gommata Betta and the multi-tiered Chaturmukha Basadi.
how_to_reach: ~38 km from Udupi and ~50 km from Mangaluru; frequent express buses connect.
heritage_era: Bhairarasa Dynasty (1432 CE, King Veera Pandya)
local_craft: Stone sculpting and copper utensils
cultural_note: The Chaturmukha Basadi is built symmetrically with four identical stone entrances and 108 pillars.

phrases.english: How far is the Chaturmukha Basadi?

name: St. Mary's Island & Malpe
short_description: A geological marvel of hexagonal columnar basaltic rock formations jutting out of the Arabian Sea, accessible by ferry from Malpe harbour.
how_to_reach: Ferry operates from Malpe Beach, ~6 km west of Udupi town center.
heritage_era: Prehistoric Deccan Volcanism (Declared National Geological Monument)
local_craft: Marine fishing net craft at Malpe harbour
cultural_note: Formed when Madagascar split from the Indian plate during sub-aerial volcanic activity 88 million years ago.

phrases.english: When does the last boat return from the island?

name: Udupi Car Street & Temples
short_description: The Dvaita philosophical heart of Karnataka, famed for the 13th-century Sri Krishna Matha, Kanakana Kindi window, and eight historic Ashta Mathas.
how_to_reach: Major railhead on the Konkan Railway and hub on NH 66; ~60 km north of Mangaluru.
heritage_era: Dvaita Vedanta Founded by Sri Madhvacharya (13th century CE)
local_craft: Pure silver idol jewellery and temple chariot woodcarving
cultural_note: Saint Kanakadasa, denied entry due to his caste, was blessed when the idol of Lord Krishna turned around to face him through a crack in the wall.

festivals.name: Paryaya Utsava
festivals.note: Biennial transfer of temple worship rights among the heads of the eight Ashta Mathas.

phrases.english: Where is the viewing point for Kanakana Kindi?
phrases.when_to_use: Inside the Sri Krishna temple complex.

name: Anegudde
short_description: Hilltop temple dedicated to Lord Vinayaka (Siddhi Vinayaka) overlooking coastal coconut groves, one of seven Mukti Sthalas of Parashurama Kshetra.
how_to_reach: ~30 km north of Udupi and ~9 km south of Kundapura near Kumbhashi village.
heritage_era: Ancient Coastal Mukti Sthala tradition
local_craft: Brass bell casting
cultural_note: The name Anegudde translates to 'Elephant Hill' referring to Lord Ganesha presiding over the coastal plateau.

phrases.english: What time is the temple lunch prasaada served?
phrases.when_to_use: Around noon at the dining hall.

name: Bhatkal Old Port
short_description: Historical port town with unique coastal Nawayath heritage, medieval stone Jain basadis, Dutch graves, and old wooden houses.
how_to_reach: Major stop on Konkan Railway and NH 66; ~40 km north of Kundapura.
heritage_era: Vijayanagara, Haduvalli & Nawayath merchant era (14th–18th century CE)
local_craft: Intricate wooden balustrades and boat carpentry
cultural_note: Bhatkal was the chief seaport of the Vijayanagara Empire through which Persian warhorses were imported.

phrases.english: Where is the old port located?
phrases.when_to_use: Asking for directions near the estuary.

name: Honnavar Estuary
short_description: The serene meeting point of the Sharavathi River and the sea, known for the Kandla mangrove boardwalk, boat rides, and coastal birdlife.
how_to_reach: Located on NH 66, ~20 km north of Kumta and ~45 km south of Karwar.
heritage_era: Ancient Gersoppa estuary waterway
local_craft: Traditional canoe carving from jackfruit wood
cultural_note: The Sharavathi backwaters around Honnavar support fragile mangrove ecosystems nurtured by local fisherfolk.

phrases.english: Where is the ticket counter for the mangrove walk?

name: Sasihithlu
short_description: A pristine sandspit beach where the Pavanje and Nandini rivers converge with the Arabian Sea, prized for surf breaks and quiet sunset views.
how_to_reach: ~25 km north of Mangaluru and ~6 km off the Mukka highway turnoff.
heritage_era: Tulu Nadu coastal estuarine landscape
local_craft: Shell crafts and surfboards
cultural_note: Site of India's Open Surfing festivals, preserving an uncluttered and non-commercialized coastline.

phrases.english: Can we walk to the river confluence from here?
phrases.when_to_use: Walking on the Sasihithlu sand bar.

name: Agumbe
short_description: Known as the Cherrapunji of the South, famous for dense rainforest canopies, King Cobra research, Onake Abbi and Barkana Falls.
how_to_reach: Located atop the Agumbe Ghat on SH 65; accessible by KSRTC buses from Thirthahalli, Shivamogga, or Udupi.
heritage_era: Pre-colonial Malnad ghat passage and rainforest biosphere
local_craft: Areca nut leaf plate pressing and cane baskets
cultural_note: Setting for R.K. Narayan's televised Malgudi Days in the 1980s.

phrases.english: Are leeches common in the rain?

name: Kavaledurga
short_description: A three-tiered 9th-to-16th-century stone hill fort fortified by the Keladi Nayakas, featuring mossy ramparts and views toward Varahi backwaters.
how_to_reach: Roughly 18 km from Thirthahalli town in Shivamogga district; reached by vehicle and climb.
heritage_era: Keladi Nayaka Dynasty (16th–18th century CE)
local_craft: Hase Chittara folk wall-art motifs in the Sagar–Thirthahalli belt
cultural_note: Kavaledurga served as the final stronghold of Queen Virammaji of Keladi before the Mysuru siege in 1763.

phrases.kannada: ಕೋಟೆಯ ಮೇಲಕ್ಕೆ ಹತ್ತಲು ಎಷ್ಟು ಸಮಯ ಬೇಕು?
phrases.transliteration: Koteya melakke hattalu eshtu samaya beku?
phrases.english: How much time does it take to climb to the top of the fort?
phrases.when_to_use: At the fort entrance gate before starting the climb.

name: Ikkeri & Keladi
short_description: Twin capitals of the Keladi Nayaka kingdom; Ikkeri features the Aghoreshvara Temple, while Keladi hosts the Rameshwara Temple and museum.
how_to_reach: Located ~6–10 km from Sagar railhead in Shivamogga district; connected by local buses and auto-rickshaws.
heritage_era: Keladi Nayaka Dynasty (16th–17th century CE)
local_craft: Sandalwood and rosewood carving in Sagar town
cultural_note: Queen Chennamma of Keladi gave asylum to Rajaram Chhatrapati (son of Shivaji) here when pursued by Aurangzeb's Mughal armies.

phrases.english: Which is the road to the Aghoreshvara Temple?

name: Belur & Halebidu
short_description: Heartland of the Hoysala Empire featuring the Chennakeshava Temple at Belur and twin-shrined Hoysaleshwara complex at Halebidu.
how_to_reach: Roughly 35–40 km from Hassan railhead; frequent buses connect Hassan, Belur, and Halebidu.
heritage_era: Hoysala Empire (12th century CE, King Vishnuvardhana)
local_craft: Soapstone miniature sculpture workshops in Halebidu
cultural_note: Inscribed along the friezes are names of individual Hoysala master sculptors such as Dasoja and Chavana.

festivals.name: Hoysala Mahotsava
festivals.note: Classical dance and music festival held against the temple backdrop.

phrases.english: Please tell us about the Shilabalika bracket sculptures
phrases.when_to_use: Engaging a monument guide at Belur.

name: Jog Falls
short_description: One of India's grandest tiered waterfalls where the Sharavathi River plunges 253 metres in four distinct cascades: Raja, Roarer, Rocket, and Rani.
how_to_reach: ~30 km from Sagar town railhead; well connected by KSRTC buses.
heritage_era: Natural cataract on the Western Ghats edge
local_craft: Sandalwood oil and soapstone carvings at the tourist bazaar
cultural_note: Celebrated in Kannada poetry and landscape lore as the crown jewel of the Sahyadri mountains.

phrases.english: Are the steps open to descend to the base of the falls?
phrases.when_to_use: Inquiring at the forest viewpoint gate.

name: Mullayanagiri & Baba Budangiri
short_description: The highest peak in Karnataka (1,930 m) offering sweeping views over the coffee country, paired with the syncretic shrine of Dattatreya Peetha.
how_to_reach: ~22 km from Chikkamagaluru town; accessible by local 4x4 jeep or road.
heritage_era: Sufi Baba Budan 17th century coffee lore & sacred hills
local_craft: Artisanal coffee bean processing and wood root carvings
cultural_note: Sufi saint Baba Budan smuggled seven raw coffee beans from Yemen in his belt in the 1670s, planting them on these slopes and birthing Indian coffee.

phrases.english: Is the road to the summit in good condition?
phrases.when_to_use: Checking with jeep drivers in Chikkamagaluru.

name: Kudremukha & Kalasa
short_description: Horse-faced shola-grassland mountain peak protected inside Kudremukha National Park, paired with the sacred temple town of Kalasa on the Bhadra River.
how_to_reach: ~110 km from Mangaluru and ~85 km from Chikkamagaluru; trek requires forest department permit.
heritage_era: Shola-grassland ecology & Ancient Agasthya mythology
local_craft: Tea and organic spices packaging around Kalasa
cultural_note: Declared an international biodiversity hotspot, preserving the origin springs of the Tunga, Bhadra, and Netravati rivers.

phrases.kannada: ಚಾರಣಕ್ಕೆ ಅರಣ್ಯ ಇಲಾಖೆ ಅನುಮತಿ ಎಲ್ಲಿ ಪಡೆಯಬೇಕು?
phrases.transliteration: Charaanake aranya ilaakhe anumati elli padeyabeku?
phrases.english: Where do we obtain the forest department trek permit?

name: Sringeri
short_description: The primary southern matha established by Adi Shankaracharya on the banks of the Tunga, noted for the Vidyashankara Temple with zodiac pillars.
how_to_reach: ~85 km from Udupi and ~90 km from Chikkamagaluru; buses connect via Agumbe or Balehonnur.
heritage_era: Advaita Vedanta Founded by Adi Shankaracharya & Vijayanagara Era (14th century CE)
local_craft: Traditional Sanskrit manuscript palm-leaf keeping and bronze craft
cultural_note: The twelve pillars in the Vidyashankara Temple are sculpted with zodiac signs such that morning sunlight hits each sign in its corresponding solar month.

phrases.english: Can we feed the sacred fish in the Tunga river?
phrases.when_to_use: At the river steps behind the temple.

name: Madikeri
short_description: The misty hill capital of Kodagu, noted for the 17th-century Madikeri Fort, Raja's Seat sunset garden, Omkareshwara Temple, and coffee estates.
how_to_reach: ~120 km from Mysuru and ~135 km from Mangaluru along NH 275.
heritage_era: Haleri Rajas of Kodagu (17th–19th century CE)
local_craft: Kodagu traditional silver jewellery and hand-woven warrior daggers (Peeche Katti)
cultural_note: Unique martial and agricultural culture honoring ancestors and firearms through the Kailpodh and Puthari harvest festivals.

festivals.name: Madikeri Dasara
festivals.note: Famous night carnival with ten elaborate moving mythological tableau floats.

phrases.english: Can we see a good sunset from Raja's Seat?

name: Talakaveri & Bhagamandala
short_description: The sacred birthplace of the River Kaveri on the Brahmagiri slopes, accompanied by the river confluence and Kerala-style shrines at Bhagamandala.
how_to_reach: ~44 km west of Madikeri; accessible by road and local buses.
heritage_era: Sacred Kaveri origin traditions & Haleri kings
local_craft: Brass pooja water vessels
cultural_note: Every year on Tula Sankramana, water erupts from the small spring at a predetermined astrological moment, celebrated across Kodagu.

festivals.name: Tula Sankramana (Kaveri Theerthodbhava)
festivals.note: Holy day celebrating the perennial rebirth of River Kaveri.

phrases.english: What is the date for the holy spring resurgence?

name: Mandalpatti
short_description: A windswept grass-covered hill ridge overlooking the Pushpagiri wildlife sanctuary, famous for sea-of-clouds morning views and jeep trails.
how_to_reach: ~18 km from Madikeri; final 4 km requires local 4-wheel-drive jeep hire.
heritage_era: Sahyadri Wilderness Ridge
local_craft: Wild spice powders and raw estate coffee
cultural_note: Known in local Kodava lore as 'Mugilu-pete' or the marketplace of clouds.

phrases.english: How much is the jeep fare to the peak?

name: Kote Betta
short_description: Third highest peak in Kodagu resembling a fortress fort, offering a quiet day hike through coffee plantations and grassy ridgelines.
how_to_reach: ~30 km from Madikeri towards Somwarpet; trail starts from Hattihole village.
heritage_era: Ancient hill shrine tradition
local_craft: Local honey and pepper harvesting
cultural_note: Legend recounts that the Pandavas spent a period of their exile in these caves.

phrases.english: Is there a temple at the top of the hill?

name: Nagara Fort
short_description: The historic capital of Bidanur under Shivappa Nayaka, featuring ancient palace water tanks, watchtowers, and laterite bastions surrounded by lush hills.
how_to_reach: ~18 km from Hosanagara and ~85 km from Shivamogga city.
heritage_era: Keladi Nayaka Kingdom (1640 CE, King Shivappa Nayaka)
local_craft: Chittara folk paintings and areca-wood crafts
cultural_note: Bidanur was once so prosperous as a spice and diamond trading centre that European travelers named it the 'City of Gold'.

phrases.english: Where are the palace water pools?

name: Balligavi
short_description: Birthplace of saint Allama Prabhu and Queen Shantala, famed for the 11th-century Western Chalukya Kedareshvara Temple with filigree soapstone lattices.
how_to_reach: ~22 km from Shikaripura town and ~70 km from Shivamogga city.
heritage_era: Western Chalukya & Hoysala (11th–12th century CE)
local_craft: Sculptors' guild tradition (Dakshina Kedara school)
cultural_note: Celebrated in epigraphs as an educational hub with five great monasteries (Pancha-Mathas) imparting Vedic, Jain, and Buddhist knowledge.

phrases.english: How ancient is the Kedareshvara Temple?

name: Lakkundi
short_description: An quiet village known for Later Chalukya stone temples, ornate stepwells such as Musukina Bavi, and Brahma Jinalaya.
how_to_reach: Located near Gadag town along the Hubballi–Hosapete highway corridor; accessible by local buses or taxis from Gadag.
heritage_era: Kalyani Chalukya & Seuna (10th–12th century CE)
local_craft: Stone carving heritage and handloom cotton weaving in the broader Gadag belt
cultural_note: Lakkundi is historically associated with Daana Chintamani Attimabbe, a patron of Jain literature.

phrases.english: Which is the way to see the Musukina Bavi stepwell?
phrases.when_to_use: Locating the famous stepped well in Lakkundi.

name: Aihole
short_description: Cradle of Indian temple architecture featuring over 120 stone temples, including the apsidal Durga Temple and Lad Khan shrine.
how_to_reach: ~34 km from Badami railhead and ~14 km from Pattadakal; connected by local buses and taxis.
heritage_era: Badami Chalukya Dynasty (5th–8th century CE)
local_craft: Ilkal saris and Guledgudda khana fabric weaving in adjacent towns
cultural_note: The Meguti hill inscription in Aihole, composed by Ravikirti in 634 CE, records Pulakeshin II's victory over Harshavardhana.

phrases.english: Where are the sculptures of the Durga temple?

name: Badami
short_description: The dramatic red-sandstone capital of the Early Chalukyas, featuring four rock-cut cave temples, Bhutanatha Temple on Agastya Lake, and the north fort.
how_to_reach: Connected by Badami railway station; well linked by buses from Hubballi, Belagavi, and Bagalkote.
heritage_era: Badami Chalukya (6th–8th century CE, Pulakeshin I & successors)
local_craft: Red sandstone miniature carvings and Ilkal handloom saris
cultural_note: The cave temples carved out of the cliffface represent a synthesis of Shaiva, Vaishnava, and Jain iconography.

festivals.name: Banashankari Jathre
festivals.note: Month-long cultural fair and chariot festival at nearby Banashankari temple.

phrases.english: How many steps to reach Cave 4?

name: Dambal
short_description: An architectural wonder featuring the 24-pointed star-shaped vimana of Dodda Basappa Temple and Someshwara shrine.
how_to_reach: ~21 km south of Gadag town; accessible by local buses or hired auto-rickshaws.
heritage_era: Kalyani Chalukya (12th century CE)
cultural_note: Dambal was once a centre of Buddhist Mahayana worship as recorded in an 11th-century inscription mentioning a temple to Buddhist goddess Tara.

phrases.kannada: ದೊಡ್ಡಬಸಪ್ಪ ದೇವಸ್ಥಾನದ ನಕ್ಷತ್ರಾಕಾರದ ಗೋಪುರ ಎಲ್ಲಿಂದ ನೋಡಬೇಕು?
phrases.transliteration: Doddabasappa devasthaanada nakshatraakaarada goopura ellinda noodabeku?
phrases.english: From where is the star-shaped vimana tower best viewed?

name: Pattadakal
short_description: UNESCO World Heritage site on the Malaprabha River where Chalukya kings were coronated, showcasing harmonious coexistence of Dravidian and Nagara styles.
how_to_reach: ~22 km from Badami and ~14 km from Aihole; frequent buses connect along the circuit.
heritage_era: Badami Chalukya (7th–8th century CE, Queen Lokamahadevi era)
local_craft: Stone replica carvings and Ilkal handloom stoles
cultural_note: The grand Virupaksha Temple was commissioned by Queen Lokamahadevi in 740 CE to commemorate King Vikramaditya II's victory over the Pallavas.

festivals.name: Pattadakal Dance Festival
festivals.note: Classical dance festival organised by the Karnataka state tourism department.

phrases.kannada: ದ್ರಾವಿಡ ಮತ್ತು ನಾಗರ ಶೈಲಿಯ ನಡುವಿನ ವ್ಯತ್ಯಾಸವೇನು?
phrases.transliteration: Draavida mattu Naagara shailiya naduvina vyatyaasavenu?
phrases.english: What is the difference between the Dravidian and Nagara styles?
phrases.when_to_use: Speaking with the ASI heritage guide.

name: Mahakuta
short_description: A tranquil 7th-century forest Shaiva temple complex built around a perennial natural spring pool called Vishnu Pushkarini.
how_to_reach: ~14 km east of Badami town; accessible by local auto or road.
heritage_era: Early Chalukya Dynasty (7th century CE)
local_craft: Clay lamps and stone shivalingas
cultural_note: The Mahakuta Pillar inscription contains vital historical genealogical data of the Early Chalukya kings.

phrases.english: Is bathing permitted in the pushkarini pool?

name: Banashankari
short_description: Revered shrine of Goddess Shakambhari located in Tilakaranya forest, featuring the grand Haridra Theertha stepped tank flanked by stone watchtowers.
how_to_reach: ~5 km south of Badami on the highway towards Gadag.
heritage_era: Early Chalukya & Maratha Renovation (7th–18th century CE)
local_craft: Ilkal saris woven in neighbouring villages
cultural_note: The annual Banashankari fair brings camel and cattle trades and traditional touring drama companies.

festivals.name: Banashankari Jathre
festivals.note: Month-long historical regional trade and temple chariot fair.

phrases.english: Where are the lamp towers of Haridra Theertha?

name: Sudi
short_description: Historic town featuring the 11th-century Jodu Kalasa (Twin Towered) Gudi, Mallikarjuna Temple, and stepwells built under Western Chalukya princess Akkadevi.
how_to_reach: ~30 km from Gajendragad and ~50 km from Gadag; accessible by country roads.
heritage_era: Western Chalukya Dynasty (11th century CE)
local_craft: Khadi handloom weaving
cultural_note: Akkadevi, a Western Chalukya princess celebrated for administrative and military skill ('Gunada Bedagi'), administered the Kisukadu division from Sudi.

phrases.english: Where is the Twin Towered temple?

name: Kittur
short_description: The courageous citadel of Rani Chennamma, home to the ruined palace fortress, museum of armaments, and statues honoring the 1824 revolt against the British East India Company.
how_to_reach: Located directly on NH 48, ~48 km from Belagavi and ~30 km from Dharwad.
heritage_era: Kittur Principality (18th–19th century CE)
local_craft: Brass armaments and traditional handloom
cultural_note: Rani Chennamma led an armed rebellion against the British doctrine of lapse 33 years before the 1857 revolt.

festivals.name: Kittur Utsav
festivals.note: Annual state celebration commemorating Rani Chennamma's victory against British forces.

phrases.english: Where is the Rani Chennamma museum?

name: Savadatti
short_description: Ancient capital of the Ratta dynasty featuring an 18th-century stone fort with eight bastions and nearby pilgrimage hill shrine of Yellamma (Renuka).
how_to_reach: ~78 km from Belagavi city and ~38 km from Dharwad; connected by state buses.
heritage_era: Ratta Dynasty & Maratha era (9th–18th century CE)
local_craft: Handloom cotton saris and temple brassware
cultural_note: Yellamma Gudda attracts millions of devotees from Karnataka, Maharashtra, and Andhra Pradesh for Banada Hunnime.

phrases.english: How is the view from top of the fort?

name: Halasi
short_description: One of the oldest historic capitals of the Kadambas of Banavasi, housing the 5th-century Bhoo Varaha Narasimha Temple with towering black stone idols.
how_to_reach: ~14 km from Khanapur railhead and ~40 km from Belagavi city.
heritage_era: Kadamba Dynasty (5th–12th century CE)
local_craft: Wood carving and rural agriculture
cultural_note: The Kadamba dynasty of Halasi played a formative role in early Kannada epigraphy and temple architecture.

phrases.english: Where are the ancient Kadamba sculptures?

name: Gokak Falls
short_description: A horseshoe waterfall on the Ghataprabha River plunging over red sandstone cliffs, crossed by a 201-metre pedestrian hanging suspension bridge.
how_to_reach: ~6 km from Gokak town and ~65 km north-east of Belagavi city.
heritage_era: 19th century industrial heritage (1887 CE) & Chalukya rock shrines
local_food: Gokak Karadantu (fried edible gum sweet with dry fruits)
local_craft: GI-tagged Gokak Karadantu sweet manufacturing guilds
cultural_note: Known as Karnataka's Niagara, the site features one of India's earliest hydro-electric generating stations established in 1887.

phrases.english: Is there a fee to walk on the suspension bridge?

name: Chaudayyadanapura
short_description: A jewel of Western Chalukya architecture on the banks of the Tungabhadra River, famed for the Mukteshwara Temple and Sharanas' vachana heritage.
how_to_reach: ~18 km from Ranebennur railhead and ~45 km from Haveri town.
heritage_era: Kalyani Chalukya (11th–12th century CE)
local_craft: Red Byadgi chilli trading and cotton grading
cultural_note: Associated with 12th-century vachana poet Shivasharana Ambigara Chaudayya, a boatman-philosopher of the Sharana movement.

phrases.kannada: ಮುಕ್ತೇಶ್ವರ ದೇವಾಲಯದ ನದಿಯ ದಡಕ್ಕೆ ದಾರಿ ಎಲ್ಲಿದೆ?
phrases.transliteration: Mukteshwara devaalayada nadiya dadakke daari ellide?
phrases.english: Where is the path to the riverbank from the temple?

name: Hampi
short_description: UNESCO World Heritage site across a surreal boulder landscape, capital of the Vijayanagara Empire featuring the stone chariot at Vijaya Vittala and Virupaksha Temple.
how_to_reach: ~12 km from Hosapete junction railhead; well connected by overnight trains and buses from Bengaluru and Hyderabad.
heritage_era: Vijayanagara Empire (14th–16th century CE)
local_craft: Banana-fibre bags and stone replica carving in Anegundi & Kamalapura
cultural_note: Historically known as Kishkindha in the Ramayana; grew to become the second-largest city in the medieval world around 1500 CE.

festivals.name: Hampi Utsav
festivals.note: Mega state cultural festival featuring music, light shows on monuments, and fireworks.

phrases.english: Which is the way to the stone chariot?

name: Bidar Fort & Bahmani Monuments
short_description: Deccan capital fortified with a triple-layered moat carved from red laterite rock, housing Rangin Mahal, Tarkash Mahal, and Solah Khamba Mosque.
how_to_reach: Connected by Bidar railway station; ~140 km from Hyderabad and accessible by state buses from Kalaburagi.
heritage_era: Bahmani Sultanate & Barid Shahi (15th–16th century CE)
local_craft: GI-tagged Bidriware (zinc-copper alloy inlaid with pure silver)
cultural_note: Bidar was known as the 'Crown of the Deccan' with sophisticated Persian Karez underground water networks.

festivals.name: Bidar Utsav
festivals.note: Heritage festival with kite flying on fort ramparts and Ghazal recitals.

phrases.english: Where are the Bidri craft workshops?
phrases.when_to_use: Near Siddiq Talim in old Bidar town.

name: Sannati & Kanaganahalli
short_description: Archaeological treasure on the Bhima River where excavations revealed a Great Stupa and the only known inscribed portrait stone relief of Emperor Ashoka ('Raya Asoko').
how_to_reach: ~70 km from Kalaburagi and ~20 km from Nalwar railway station; reached by taxi or local bus.
heritage_era: Maurya & Shatavahana (3rd century BCE–3rd century CE)
local_craft: Limestone archaeological relief tradition
cultural_note: Discovered accidentally in 1986 when the roof of the Chandralamba temple collapsed, revealing Asokan rock edicts.

phrases.english: Where is the sculpture of Emperor Ashoka?

name: Mahmud Gawan Madrasa
short_description: A monumental 15th-century theological university with a surviving minaret adorned in Persian turquoise and yellow glazed tiles, founded by Prime Minister Mahmud Gawan.
how_to_reach: Located in the heart of old Bidar city; walking distance from the main bazaar.
heritage_era: Bahmani Sultanate (1472 CE)
local_craft: Bidriware silver inlay pens and inkwells
cultural_note: Its library once housed over 3,000 priceless illuminated manuscripts gathered from across the Islamic world.

phrases.english: Where can the remaining colored glazed tiles be seen?

name: Ashtur Royal Tombs
short_description: Row of twelve colossal domed mausoleums set in peaceful open countryside, featuring the tomb of Ahmad Shah Wali with Quranic gold-leaf calligraphy.
how_to_reach: ~4 km east of Bidar city center; reached easily by auto-rickshaw.
heritage_era: Bahmani Dynasty (15th century CE)
local_craft: Laterite masonry
cultural_note: Ahmad Shah Wali's tomb is revered by both Muslims as a Wali (saint) and by Lingayats who hold an annual Urs.

phrases.kannada: ಚಿನ್ನದ ಬಣ್ಣದ ಕ್ಯಾಲಿಗ್ರಫಿ ಇರುವ ಸಮಾಧಿ ಯಾವುದು?
phrases.transliteration: Chinnada bannada calligraphy iruva samaadhi yaavudu?
phrases.english: Which tomb has the gold calligraphy?
phrases.when_to_use: Looking for Ahmad Shah Wali's tomb.

name: Kalaburagi Fort & Jami Masjid
short_description: 14th-century fortress featuring 15 towers and the unique Jami Masjid (1367 CE), built with no open courtyard and covered by 68 domes.
how_to_reach: Located in Kalaburagi city, ~3 km from the main railway station.
heritage_era: Bahmani Sultanate (Alauddin Bahman Shah, 14th century CE)
local_craft: Wood block printing and leather footwear
cultural_note: The Jami Masjid's vaulted layout was designed by Spanish-Moorish architect Rafi of Kazvin, resembling the Great Mosque of Córdoba.

phrases.kannada: ಜಾಮಿ ಮಸೀದಿಯ ಗುಮ್ಮಟಗಳನ್ನು ನೋಡಲು ದಾರಿ ಯಾವುದು?
phrases.transliteration: Jami maseediya gummadagalannu noodalu daari yaavudu?
phrases.english: Which is the way to view the domes of the Jami Masjid?

name: Khwaja Bande Nawaz Dargah
short_description: The revered Sufi shrine of Hazrat Khwaja Syed Muhammad Gesudaraz, an oasis of spiritual syncretism built in Indo-Saracenic and Bahmani architectural style.
how_to_reach: Located ~2 km from Kalaburagi central bus stand.
heritage_era: Early 15th century CE Sufi Chisti tradition
local_craft: Incense making and attar perfumery
cultural_note: Gesudaraz wrote extensively in Dakhani Urdu and promoted communal harmony between communities across the Deccan.

festivals.name: Urs of Bande Nawaz
festivals.note: Major annual gathering drawing hundreds of thousands of pilgrims of all faiths.

phrases.english: Where is the dargah's library?

name: Malkhed & Sedam
short_description: The imperial capital Manyakheta of the Rashtrakuta Empire on the Kagina River, praised by Arab geographers as one of the four great empires of the world.
how_to_reach: ~40 km southeast of Kalaburagi; accessible by passenger train to Malkhed Road or state bus.
heritage_era: Rashtrakuta Empire (9th–10th century CE, King Amoghavarsha I)
local_craft: Sedam limestone quarrying and polishing (Shahabad stone)
cultural_note: King Amoghavarsha I patronized Kavirajamarga (c. 850 CE), the earliest available work on Kannada poetics.

phrases.english: Where is the Rashtrakuta fort located?
phrases.when_to_use: Asking along the Kagina river bridge.

name: Anegundi
short_description: Older than Hampi across the Tungabhadra, identified with mythical Kishkindha, featuring Anjanadri Hill, prehistoric rock art, and Pampa Sarovara.
how_to_reach: ~5 km from Hampi across the Tungabhadra River bridge or via coracle ferry.
heritage_era: Prehistoric iron-age rock art to Vijayanagara (14th century CE)
local_craft: Banana-fibre weaving cooperative workshops by local women
cultural_note: Anjanadri Hill in Anegundi is traditionally worshipped as the birthplace of Lord Hanuman.

phrases.english: How many steps to Anjanadri Hill?

name: Kuknur
short_description: A cluster of nine stone shrines from the 9th-century Rashtrakuta and Kalyani Chalukya eras, featuring early Kannada inscriptions and Mahamaya Temple.
how_to_reach: ~28 km from Koppal and ~12 km from Itagi; reached by rural roads.
heritage_era: Rashtrakuta & Early Kalyani Chalukya (9th–10th century CE)
local_craft: Traditional stone chiselling
cultural_note: Demonstrates the crucial transition from Rashtrakuta vimanas to the evolved ornate style of the Later Chalukyas.

phrases.english: Which is the temple with nine lingas?

name: Itagi
short_description: Hailed in its own stone inscription as 'Devalaya Chakravarti' (Emperor among Temples), built in 1112 CE with breathtaking soapstone carvings.
how_to_reach: ~22 km from Kuknur and ~35 km from Gadag or Koppal.
heritage_era: Kalyani Chalukya Empire (1112 CE, Mahadeva Dandanayaka)
local_craft: Chloritic schist relief carving
cultural_note: The temple inscription explicitly proclaims itself as the greatest temple achievement of the Western Chalukyan empire.

phrases.english: Where is the 'Emperor of Temples' inscription carved?
phrases.when_to_use: Examining the stone slab inside the hall.

name: Kanakagiri
short_description: Known locally by the Kannada proverb 'Eyes that have seen Kanakagiri need not see Kashi', noted for the spacious Kanakachalapathi temple and ornate stepwell.
how_to_reach: ~20 km from Gangavathi and ~45 km from Hosapete.
heritage_era: Vijayanagara Feudatories (16th–17th century CE)
local_craft: Stone water trough sculpting
cultural_note: Historical Suvarnagiri mentioned in Ashokan edicts of the 3rd century BCE as the seat of the Mauryan southern viceroyalty.

phrases.english: Where is the Kanakagiri stepped tank?

name: Daroji Bear Sanctuary
short_description: Asia's first dedicated sloth bear sanctuary nestled among the boulder hills near Hampi, where bears can be observed in their natural habitat from a watchtower.
how_to_reach: ~15 km from Hampi and ~20 km from Hosapete.
heritage_era: Protected scrub forest sanctuary (Established 1994)
local_craft: Scrub-jungle honey collection
cultural_note: Sloth bears forage for termites, wild berries, and honeycombs across the rocky scrub caves.

phrases.english: Is the evening time best to sight the bears?

name: Sandur
short_description: A valley nestled between mineral-rich iron-red hills, home to the 8th-to-11th-century Kumaraswamy and Parvathi temples and Lambani tribal embroidery.
how_to_reach: ~30 km from Hosapete and ~45 km from Ballari city.
heritage_era: Badami Chalukya & Rashtrakuta (8th–11th century CE) & Ghorpade Kingdom
local_craft: GI-tagged Sandur Lambani embroidery with mirrors and cowrie shells
cultural_note: Mahatma Gandhi visited Sandur in 1934 and remarked: 'See Sandur in September', admiring its green hill contours.

phrases.english: Where is the Lambani embroidery craft center?
phrases.when_to_use: Seeking the craft artisan guild in Sandur.
